# A raw tree-row batch is lost after re-add and reprojection

Please comment to claim before starting; check current assignees and linked PRs.

## Context

A Turbo Mode `TreeStore` can visibly accept a raw row batch, then restore an older value when the tree reprojects. Found while reviewing #20989; it reproduces on both its base `c78adac361a8894d563bbaae800e9fdc5f9621c2` and head `3f32b2283c6f68b59a7c953d328d7c16fcffc467`. It is inherited debt, not a blocker introduced by that PR.

Design authority: `Store#updateRows` writes a held raw row’s own data in place, and `TreeStore`’s Structural Layer retains the complete population while its visible layer is a projection. A later sort must not undo an accepted value.

## The Problem

Using the normal Neo unit setup, `Neo` plus core exports, `TreeStore` and a `TreeModel` with String `id/name` and Integer `score`:

```javascript
const store = Neo.create(TreeStore, {
    autoInitRecords: false,
    model: TestTreeModel,
    data: [
        {id: 'a', name: 'A', score: 1},
        {id: 'b', name: 'B', score: 2}
    ]
});
await store.ready();
store.add({id: 'a', name: 'A readded', score: 1}, false);
store.updateRows([{key: 'a', values: {name: 'A batched'}}]);
// The raw visible row now says 'A batched'. Do not call get() here.
store.sorters = [{property: 'score', reapplyOnRecordChange: true}];
// Reprojection/get now says 'A readded': the batch is lost.
store.destroy();
```

The source-bound probe loaded complete exact-head Store/RecordFactory/TreeStore modules, checked other imports against each immutable Git tree, and used real instances. Both refs lose the value. The existing hydration repair can hide this: calling `get()` before reprojecting heals the identity split, so a test that does so misses the raw path.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/data/TreeStore.mjs`: Structural Layer, visible projection and re-add/reprojection handoff.
- `src/collection/Base.mjs`: keyed replacement and visible item identity.
- `src/data/RecordFactory.mjs`: hydration can reconcile the two identities.
- `src/data/Store.mjs`: `updateRows` must keep the raw batch raw.

Closed #17855 corrected duplicate hierarchy entries; PR #18030 explicitly retained stale projection objects as follow-up. #20568 / #20569 heal during hydration and leave Collection replacement semantics outside their scope. None owns this unhydrated batch → reprojection loss.

## The Fix

Repair the existing re-add/identity handoff at the owning Collection/TreeStore writer so the current raw row remains authoritative across projection changes. Read those existing methods at intake; no new module or provider is proposed. Preserve the batch’s non-hydrating path and the hierarchy’s key/count invariants.

### Contract Ledger Matrix

| Surface | Authority | Required behavior | Fallback / docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TreeStore re-add/current row | TreeStore Structural Layer and Collection keyed replacement | One current row/value survives structural and visible projection access | Existing API; TreeStore guide | Re-add produces the divergence used above |
| `Store#updateRows` | Its JSDoc / Turbo Mode contract | Accepted raw data survives sort/filter reprojection | No forced hydration | Base and head source-bound reproducer |
| Hydration | RecordFactory and #20568 | Continue healing/returning the current identity without being necessary to preserve a batch | Existing API | `get()` is a positive masking control, not the fix |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The raw re-add → batch → sort sequence retains `A batched`, with no intervening `get()` or hydration.
- [ ] Filter reprojection also preserves the current row/value; structural and visible reads agree.
- [ ] Repeated re-add keeps one hierarchy entry per key and correct child/sibling counts.
- [ ] Same-object re-add and hydrated-record paths retain their behavior; raw batch edits hydrate no row.
- [ ] A focused guard fails the named base and passes the fix using the repository’s explicit unit configuration.

## Out of Scope

Numeric-parent coercion (#20913 / #20995), the single-edit 401-filter cascade, container migration (#20974), and #20989’s separate dependency-path regression. No grid repaint workaround or new identity registry.

## Avoided Traps

Do not call `get()` merely to make the test pass; do not write the stale Structural Layer while leaving a newer visible row, or the reverse. Preserve one current identity through the existing owner rather than choosing a map per caller.

### @neo-gpt-emmy - 2026-11-16T16:29:12Z

I ran both submitted fixes against the same three controls, then ran the controls on a clean Git merge of their two heads. The rows start as three raw root siblings `a,b,c`, with scores 1, 2 and 3.

| Revision | Mixed batch, observer sorts then reads `a` | Re-add raw `a,c` together without sorting | Existing hydrated `a` keeps its identity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dev@e5388567ae` | Observer and final read lose the new name | Visible names stay stale | No |
| #21009 `d96e471611` | Observer and final read both return the new name, score 9 | Flat order becomes `a,c,b`. Structural order is `a,b,c` and structural `c` keeps its old name | No |
| #21035 `17d04e974e` | Observer and final read both lose the new name | Visible names stay stale | No |
| Combined, tree `391b0d5b64` | Same result as #21009 | Same failure as #21009 | No |

The mixed batch reports zero errors on all four runs. #21009 gives the working control for the publication problem raised on #21035. Simply combining the source patches leaves two independent failures. A revision can be compared with either submission using the same probe below.

<details><summary>Reproduce in an Engine checkout with its dependencies installed</summary>

Save this as `compare-tree.mjs` and run `node compare-tree.mjs .` from the checkout. The read of `_items` inspects the flat projection without hydrating it.

```js
import path from 'node:path';
import {pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';

const root = path.resolve(process.argv[2]);
const file = relative => pathToFileURL(path.join(root, relative)).href;
const {setup} = await import(file('test/playwright/setup.mjs'));
const {default:Neo} = await import(file('src/Neo.mjs'));
await import(file('src/core/_export.mjs'));
await import(file('src/manager/Instance.mjs'));
setup({neoConfig:{unitTestMode:true}, appConfig:{name:'CompareTreeStore',isMounted:()=>true,vnodeInitialising:false}});
const {default:TreeStore} = await import(file('src/data/TreeStore.mjs'));
const {default:TreeModel} = await import(file('src/data/TreeModel.mjs'));
const {default:RecordFactory} = await import(file('src/data/RecordFactory.mjs'));
class NodeModel extends TreeModel {
    static config = {className:'Test.CompareRawBatch.Node',fields:[{name:'id',type:'String'},{name:'name',type:'String'},{name:'score',type:'Integer'}]}
}
const model=Neo.setupClass(NodeModel);
async function withTree(fn) {
    const store=Neo.create(TreeStore,{autoInitRecords:false,model,data:['a','b','c'].map((id,index)=>({id,name:id.toUpperCase(),score:index+1}))});
    try {await store.ready();return await fn(store)} finally {store.destroy()}
}
const results={};
results.mixedPublication=await withTree(store=>{
    store.sorters=[{property:'score'}];store.get('b');
    store.add({id:'a',name:'A readded',score:9},false);
    let once=false, seen;
    store.on('recordChange',()=>{if(once)return;once=true;store.sort();const a=store.get('a');seen=[a.name,a.score]});
    const out=store.updateRows([{key:'a',values:{name:'A batched'}},{key:'b',values:{score:22}}]);
    const a=store.get('a');return {seen,final:[a.name,a.score],errors:out.errors.length};
});
results.multiReplace=await withTree(store=>{
    store.add([{id:'a',name:'A2',score:9},{id:'c',name:'C2',score:11}],false);
    return {flat:store._items.map(it=>[it.id,it.name]),structural:store.getChildren('root').map(it=>[it.id,it.name]),hydrated:store._items.filter(it=>RecordFactory.isRecord(it)).map(it=>it.id)};
});
results.hydratedIdentity=await withTree(store=>{
    const first=store.get('a');store.add({id:'a',name:'A readded',score:9},false);
    store.updateRows([{key:'a',values:{name:'A batched'}}]);store.sorters=[{property:'score'}];
    const last=store.get('a'); return {same:last===first,final:[last.name,last.score]};
});
console.log(JSON.stringify(results));
```
